title.en: Advancing Professional Standards through the 4th ASCEND Assessment
title.zh: 通过第四届 ASCEND 能力评估推进专业标准建设

summary.en: Hosted by the
summary.zh: 2026年10月5–8日，来自东盟各国的19名灾害管理专业人员在文莱斯里巴加湾参加第四届 ASCEND 能力评估，考核涵盖快速评估、人道主义物流、信息管理和水环卫（WASH）四大专业领域。

content.en:
Held from 5-8 October 2026 in Bandar Seri Begawan, Brunei Darussalam, 19 disaster management professionals from across ASEAN gathered for the 4th ASCEND Competency Assessment. As part of the assessment, candidates underwent face-to-face evaluations across four professional competency areas: Rapid Assessment, Humanitarian Logistics, Information Management, and WASH.
Hosted by the
National Disaster Management Centre (NDMC) of Brunei Darussalam
, the assessment was followed by an After-Action Review (AAR) Workshop, where assessors and experts reflected on lessons learned, explored ways to strengthen quality assurance mechanisms, and reviewed proposed Continuing Professional Development (CPD) pathways to support future certification renewal and the continuous growth of ASCEND-certified professionals.
The AHA Centre extends its sincere appreciation to the Government of the Republic of Korea, through the
ASEAN-Korea Cooperation Fund (AKCF)
, for its continued support in advancing capacity building in disaster management for a stronger and more resilient disaster management community across ASEAN.
Learn more:
https://ascend.ahacentre.org/
content.zh: 2026年10月5日至8日，第四届 ASCEND 能力评估在文莱达鲁萨兰国斯里巴加湾举行，来自东盟各国的19名灾害管理专业人员齐聚文莱。评估期间，候选人在快速评估、人道主义物流、信息管理和水环卫（WASH）四个专业能力领域接受面对面考核。本次评估由文莱国家灾害管理中心（NDMC）主办，考核后举行了事后复盘（AAR）研讨会，评估专家共同总结经验、探讨强化质量保障机制的路径，并审议了拟议的持续职业发展（CPD）路径方案。

OVERVIEW
Continuous heavy to very heavy rainfall over Thailand, driven by a monsoon trough over the Central region combined with a strong Southwest Monsoon prevailing over the Andaman Sea and the Gulf of Thailand, has caused widespread flooding in recent days as water flowing down from the North merged with existing water volumes in the Central region. As of 26 September 2026 at 0600 HRS UTC+7, flooding has been reported across 22 provinces, including Bangkok, according to the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (
DDPM
) and the Thai Meteorological Department (
TMD
).
.

DDPM

22 provinces affected: Chiang Mai, Phetchabun, Nakhon Sawan, Phitsanulok, Uthai Thani, Lop Buri, Sing Buri, Suphan Buri, Saraburi, Pathum Thani, Nakhon Pathom, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, Samut Prakan, Prachin Buri, Chachoengsao, Sa Kaeo, Chon Buri, Rayong, Chanthaburi, Trat, Nakhon Ratchasima, and Bangkok
93 districts, 350 sub-districts, and 1,425 villages affected, with 27,109 households (84,605 people) affected

The visit brings together 22 (twenty-two) middle managers from National Disaster Management Offices (NDMOs) and other related officials from all 11 (eleven) ASEAN Member States (AMS) to not only learn from Japan’s best practices in disaster risk reduction and management but also exchange experience on the subject.
The Study Visit marks the culmination of an intensive learning journey under the ACE-LEDMP Middle Executive Level – Third Batch, a leadership programme supported by the Government of Japan through the Japan-ASEAN Integration Fund (JAIF). Prior to their visit to Japan, participants completed one month of online learning and one month of on-site sessions in Jakarta, where they strengthened their understanding of disaster leadership, emergency management, humanitarian coordination, and regional disaster management mechanisms.
Co-organised by the AHA Centre and Kobe-based Asia Disaster Reduction Center (ADRC), the Study Visit provides an opportunity to translate classroom learning into practical insights through direct engagement with institutions and practitioners at the forefront of disaster management. content.en:
OVERVIEW
:
At 0458 HRS UTC+7 on 15 August 2026,
BMKG
reported a M7.7 earthquake occurred offshore approximately 30 km northeast of Mbay, Nagekeo Regency, East Nusa Tenggara (NTT).
BMKG
advisory indicated that tsunami is possible for Indonesia, particularly for several coastal areas over East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara, South Sulawesi, and Southeast Sulawesi. The tsunami advisory was ended at 0731 HRS.
BMKG
reported observed tsunami waves ranging from 0.17–0.94 m in height. Meanwhile, as of 0707 HRS UTC+7,
BMKG
had recorded 37 aftershocks ranging from M3.6 to M6.2. Data collection and damage assessments are ongoing.

According to
BMKG
, the strongest reported shaking included:
Aesesa (Nagekeo), Riung (Ngada), and Mbay: approximately VII MMI, with residents reportedly rushing out of buildings and minor structural damage occurring. Wolowae and Bajawa: approximately VI MMI; and Ende, Borong, and Ruteng: approximately V MMI.
The earthquake was also felt across Flores, parts of Sumba, Adonara, and Solor, and some parts in West Nusa Tenggara.
IMPACTS AND DAMAGES
:
BNPB
reported that the earthquake was strongly felt across several areas, from Nusa Tenggara Islands to southern parts of Sulawesi. As of 08:38 WIB,
BNPB
has reported 2 fatalities and 1 injured person in Sikka Regency, associated with impacts around the El Say Port area. Structural damage has also been reported in Sikka and other affected areas.
Sikka Regency/Maumere: Structural damage, including building collapse, has been reported in Maumere. Impacts were reported around El Say Port, where casualties were recorded. Damage to buildings and port-related facilities has also been reported.
Nagekeo and Central/Northern Flores: Strong shaking of up to approximately VII MMI was reported around Mbay/Aesesa.

title.en: 15 ASEAN-ERAT Members Complete Level 2 Course on Early Recovery
title.zh: 15名 ASEAN-ERAT 成员完成早期恢复二级课程

summary.en: Through hands-on exercises, knowledge sharing, and field visits to earthquake recovery sites, participants gained valuable insights into translating recovery needs into practical actions that support communities affected by disasters.
summary.zh: 2026年8月3–7日，来自东南亚各地的15名 ASEAN-ERAT 成员在缅甸内比都参加由缅甸灾害管理局主办的 ASEAN-ERAT 早期恢复二级课程。

content.en:
On 3-7 August 2026, 15 ASEAN-ERAT members from across Southeast Asia gathered in Nay Pyi Taw, Myanmar, for the ASEAN-ERAT Level 2 Course on Early Recovery hosted by the Myanmar Department of Disaster Management.
Through hands-on exercises, knowledge sharing, and field visits to earthquake recovery sites, participants gained valuable insights into translating recovery needs into practical actions that support communities affected by disasters.
By investing in specialised expertise, ASEAN continues to strengthen collective disaster response and recovery in the spirit of One ASEAN, One Response.
content.zh: 2026年8月3日至7日，来自东南亚各地的15名 ASEAN-ERAT 成员齐聚缅甸内比都，参加由缅甸灾害管理局主办的 ASEAN-ERAT 早期恢复二级课程。通过实操演练、知识分享和地震恢复现场考察，学员深入学习如何将恢复需求转化为支持受灾社区的实际行动。东盟以 One ASEAN, One Response 精神持续加强集体灾害响应与恢复能力建设。

content.en:
Following the launch of cooperation between the AHA Centre and the
International Telecommunication Union
in Bangkok on 17 July 2026, the AHA Centre officially received emergency telecommunications equipment on 5 August 2026. The equipment was formally received by Mr Somsanith Ninthavong, Director of Corporate Affairs, as part of an initiative to improve disaster preparedness across ASEAN.
Pre-positioned at the AHA Centre for use throughout the region, the equipment will support emergency deployments, simulation exercises, training and capacity-building activities involving ASEAN-ERAT and ASEAN Member States. This initiative puts the new cooperation into action by helping communities stay connected during emergencies.

content.en:
OVERVIEW

PAGASA

content.en:

content.en:
On 29 July 2026, the AHA Centre and New Zealand officially launched the Strengthening Institutional Capacity of ASEAN in Disaster Management (SICAP) Phase II Project.
As one of the most significant investments in enhancing disaster management capacities across ASEAN, SICAP II will strengthen the AHA Centre’s role as a regional knowledge hub while advancing ASEAN’s position as a global leader in disaster management.
The launch was officiated by Executive Director Mr. Lee Yam Ming alongside H.E. Joanna Jane Anderson, Ambassador of New Zealand to ASEAN, H.E. San Lwin, Deputy Secretary-General of ASEAN for Socio-Cultural Community, and Dr. Raditya Jati, S.Si., M.Si., Deputy Minister for Systems and Strategy of BNPB Indonesia, witnessed by representatives of the AHA Centre Governing Board, ASEAN Secretariat, and Partners.
The AHA Centre extends its sincere appreciation to the Government of New Zealand for its continued partnership through the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT).
content.zh: 2026年7月29日，AHA中心与新西兰正式启动「加强东盟灾害管理机构能力」（SICAP）二期项目。作为提升东盟灾害管理能力最重要的投资之一，SICAP 二期将强化 AHA 中心作为区域知识枢纽的作用，同时推进东盟在全球灾害管理领域的领先地位。启动仪式由 AHA 中心执行主任李育民、新西兰驻东盟大使 Joanna Jane Anderson 阁下、东盟社会文化共同体副秘书长 San Lwin 阁下及印尼 BNPB 系统与战略事务副部长 Raditya Jati 博士共同主持。

title.zh: 闪报第1号：菲律宾萨兰加尼 M7.8 地震（2026年6月8日）

summary.en: On 08 June 2026,
summary.zh: 2026年6月8日06时37分（UTC+7），PHIVOLCS 报告棉兰老岛南部萨兰加尼 Maasim 以南32公里海域发生 M7.8 地震（震源深度33公里），初始 M7.0 后修订。将军市最高烈度 VII，曾发布海啸预警。

content.en:
OVERVIEW
On 08 June 2026,
PHIVOLCS
reported a magnitude 7.8 earthquake (depth 33 km) at 0637 HRS UTC+7 (0737 HRS local PH time), with the epicentre located 32 km south (S04°W) of Maasim, Sarangani Province, offshore southern Mindanao. The earthquake was initially recorded at magnitude 7.0 with a depth of 10 km before being upgraded in a second advisory to magnitude 7.8 at a depth of 33 km.
PHIVOLCS
assessed the quake as tectonic in origin,
with damage and aftershocks expected
. The strongest reported intensity was Intensity VII in the City of General Santos.
TSUNAMI
:
PHIVOLCS
raised a tsunami warning, advising that wave heights of more than one metre above normal tides were expected, with first waves arriving between 0737 and 0937 HRS local time and potentially continuing for hours. Residents of at least nine Mindanao provinces were advised to evacuate coastal areas immediately.
BMKG
also issued a tsunami warning for the Maluku Islands, Sulawesi and Kalimtantan. Indonesia’s BMKG reported sea-level changes of less than one metre so far.
IMPACTS AND DAMAGES
:
NDRRMC
Philippines and
BNPB
Indonesia are currently conducting initial assessments to gather information on impacts and damages.
Initial news reports show damaged buildings and infrastructures.
RESPONSE
EFFORTS
:
The Philippine President directed all relevant government agencies to act immediately and urged residents in affected provinces to move to higher ground, stating the national government is coordinating with regional offices and local chief executives.
NDRRMC
Philippines is conducting an emergency coordination meeting on the initial impact reports and the ongoing response operations. The NDRRMEOC is on
RED
alert.
Several ASEAN Member States indicated readiness to support through the AHA Centre.
